summary: Jeffrey Newmark works in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University until 1996 and at the University of British Columbia until 2009, and held a post at the University of Winnipeg.

Jeffrey S. Lidke works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held posts at Berry College, Bard College (attested 2002), and the University of Virginia (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang and studied under W. S. Karunatillake, later serving at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University, the California Culinary Academy, and Princeton University (PhD), where he was a professor from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at UNC Wilmington, UT Knoxville, and UCLA (PhD under Gregory Schopen, also studying under James L. Fitzgerald), and held teaching appointments at UCLA and UC San Diego in 2013.

Jenkuan Shih specializes in Buddhist studies. Shih earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where doctoral supervisors were Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, after completing an MA supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa.
Jennifer Cover works in Indology and religious studies. She held posts at the Australian National University (attested 2006) and at the University of Sydney as a PhD student (attested 2006–2008).

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history and archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at the University of California, Los Angeles, serving as assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jenny Hung works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and sinology. She earned a PhD from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and another from Lingnan University, serving as Assistant Professor in Humanities at HKUST.

Jens Augspurger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London. He has held positions at SOAS, IU International University of Applied Sciences, and the University of Mannheim.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held professorships at the University of Oslo (2003) and the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (around 2003).

Jens Peter Laut specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He served at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and held a post at the University of Göttingen from around 2008 to 2020.

Jens Schlieter works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Vienna and Bonn (PhD under Josef Simon) and held posts at Urania Berlin, Bonn, Bayreuth, and Bern, where he became Professor for Theory of Religion.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at Munich and Göttingen, he held professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Free University of Berlin, alongside posts at Munich, Göttingen, and two academies of sciences.

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim studied under Rosemary Smith and completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011 under the supervision of Youngsook Pak.

Jerome Silbergeld is an art historian and sinologist educated at Stanford and the University of Oregon. He held professorships and chair positions at the University of Washington (1975–2001) and Princeton University (2001–2018).

Jervoise Athelstane Baines was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Rugby School, Trinity College, Cambridge, and Trinity College Dublin, and served as a Governor of the London School of Economics in 1901.

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist and member of the Polish Academy of Sciences. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań, where he headed the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics and served as Professor from 1977 to 1991.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a linguist and Indologist. After studying in Vienna, Lviv, and under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Theodor Bloch, he served as professor at the universities of Lviv, Breslau, and the Jagiellonian University.
Jesse Ross Knutson is an Indology scholar who studied under Luis González-Reimann in 1996 and held an affiliate faculty position at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa in 2013.
